sections.name: legal balls
sections.title: Over parsing, formatting and rates
sections.what: Checks conversion from overs text to balls and back, rejects overs with more than six balls, and checks run rate and required run rate. Returns no value when balls are zero.
sections.why: Likely reason: cricket counts balls in groups of six, so correct handling must count balls rather than do decimal math.
sections.watch_out: A zero-ball run rate returns no value. Callers must handle that case or they will show an error or blank.

summary: Checks the conversion between cricket overs, such as 10.4, and legal balls, plus run rate and required run rate.
purpose: Keeps over arithmetic correct. In cricket, 10.4 means ten overs and four balls, so it is not the decimal number ten and four tenths.
why: Likely reason: decimal arithmetic on overs gives wrong answers, so the module converts to whole balls first.
how: Checks parsing of overs text and numbers, rejects impossible overs such as 10.6, formats balls back into overs, confirms every ball count from 0 to 120 survives a round trip, and checks run rates and required run rates with bad-input errors.
inputs: Literal values written in the test.
risks: Any change to these rules changes every over display and rate in the app.
debug: If a score looks wrong on screen, call parseOvers and formatOvers with the same value. Also search for places that treat overs as decimals.
